task.description:
This is a documentation/design-exploration-only change (no lib/letflow/ implementation, no priv/repo/migrations/) -- there is no OTP idiom or supervision integrity to review, and no SECURITY-REVIEWER step (no tenant-data path touched). Your gate here is scope creep and decision-record consistency, per your own role's stated duty in docs/agents/AGENT_SYSTEM.md ('idiomatic OTP usage... supervision integrity, scope creep, and consistency with docs/migration/decisions/ records').

CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (step 2, PASS) already independently re-verified the six ISS-0439 acceptance criteria and several factual claims -- read its result.summary in handoffs/WF03-ISS0439-20260904/step-02-code-design-validator.json, but do not merely trust it; your own gate is different in kind, not a repeat of the same checks.

Specifically check:
1. SCOPE CREEP -- does docs/migration/decisions/0019-defer-1c-typed-templates.md or lib/letflow/design/iss0439-1c-taxonomy-mapping.md, anywhere, smuggle in an implicit requirement, a schema decision, or a commitment to build something? Read both in full looking specifically for this -- a design-exploration issue's own AC5 forbids it, and CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR already checked for literal requirements.yaml edits and code fences, but scope creep can also appear as prose that reads as a de facto commitment even without a formal artefact (e.g. 'REQ-ANALYST should draft the following fields...' would be creep even in prose).
2. DECISION-RECORD CONSISTENCY -- does 0019 contradict, duplicate, or drift from any existing record under docs/migration/decisions/? Specifically check it against 0004 (humanless-pipeline, since this decision references the pipeline's own governance) and confirm 0019's numbering/format genuinely matches the existing series (read at least 2 other records' structure, e.g. 0017/0018, to confirm 0019 follows the same convention -- do not just trust CODE-DESIGNER's own claim of having done this).
3. Confirm the decision record's relationship to ISS-0438's own already-resolved scoping decision (lib/letflow/design/iss0438-entity-subsystem-scoping.md SS5) is stated accurately and does not contradict what that artefact actually says -- read iss0438's SS5 yourself and compare.
4. Confirm neither artefact reopens or re-litigates ISS-0438's already-closed scoping question (that would be scope creep in the other direction -- redoing settled work).
acceptance_criteria: Explicit verdict on scope creep: PASS (no creep found) or FAIL naming the specific passage
Explicit verdict on decision-record consistency against at least 0004 and one other existing record, stating what was checked and why no contradiction exists
Confirms 0019's relationship to iss0438-entity-subsystem-scoping.md SS5 is accurately stated, having read SS5 directly rather than trusting the citation
States plainly whether this artefact is fit to serve as the durable record a future reader would find before re-proposing the 1C taxonomy idea

result.summary: REVIEWER gate for ISS-0439's two prose artefacts (scope creep + decision-record consistency only, per this issue's design-exploration-only nature -- no OTP/supervision/security review applicable). (1) SCOPE CREEP: PASS, no creep found. Read both lib/letflow/design/iss0439-1c-taxonomy-mapping.md and docs/migration/decisions/0019-defer-1c-typed-templates.md in full, specifically hunting for prose that reads as a de facto commitment even without a formal artefact. Neither drafts a schema, a requirement, an entity field list, nor directs another role to build/draft anything ('REQ-ANALYST should draft...'-style language does not appear). The mapping doc's SS4 sequencing recommendation and 0019's three review triggers are explicitly conditional/observational ('watch what tenants actually build'), not a build commitment, and are themselves required by ISS-0439's own AC2/AC6 (state a verdict, state review triggers) rather than creep beyond it. (2) DECISION-RECORD CONSISTENCY: PASS against 0004 and against the 0017/0018 format convention. Read 0004-humanless-pipeline.md in full: its producer/validator-pairing and non-silent-redecision principles are satisfied by this very run's chain (CODE-DESIGNER -> CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR -> REVIEWER) and 0019 does not touch pipeline governance/roster/merge mechanics at all, so there is no overlap capable of contradicting 0004. Read 0017-task-queue-selection-model.md and 0018-branch-protection-posture.md in full for format: both follow # NNNN title / Status+Owner line / ## Question / ## Decision / ## Consequences / ## What this record does not decide, with extra domain-specific sections as needed (0017's Evidence, 0018's Configuration to apply). 0019 matches this convention exactly (# 0019 title / Status+Owner / ## Question / ## Decision: DEFER / ## Recorded decision / ## Review triggers / ## Dependency / ## Grounding artefact / ## What this record does not decide) -- genuinely followed, not merely claimed by CODE-DESIGNER. (3) ISS-0438 SS5 RELATIONSHIP: PASS, accurately stated. Read lib/letflow/design/iss0438-entity-subsystem-scoping.md SS5 ('AC6 -- sequencing against ISS-0439', lines 409-443) directly myself. It states the port-now recommendation is 'that trigger firing in the proceed direction... not resolved, not superseded, not reopened' and that ISS-0439 'must stay exactly as filed... until real tenant usage... produces the evidence' -- porting the substrate is 'a necessary precondition... not itself sufficient grounds to revisit it.' 0019's own text ('This record's deferral is unaffected by ISS-0438's own resolution... reason (1) already anticipated exactly this state') matches this precisely; 0019 never claims SS5 resolved or superseded ISS-0439's deferral, and does not re-litigate or reopen ISS-0438's own already-closed scoping question (IN SCOPE/S6/REQ-225..231 is treated as settled and cited, not re-derived or second-guessed, in either artefact). (4) FIT AS DURABLE RECORD: yes, plainly. 0019 quotes the user's three deferral reasons verbatim (not paraphrased), states all three review triggers explicitly, cross-references its grounding artefact, states the REQ-225..231 dependency with current status independently re-verified, and gives a real verdict (SS4 of the mapping doc: sequencing recommended, not outright rejection, not a neutral hedge) rather than avoiding a position. A future reader re-proposing the 1C taxonomy idea would find the reasoning, the evidence threshold to clear, and the concrete module-level grounding here, not a blank page.
